thread:
evan: Quick note from today's roadmap huddle: customers keep asking for 'egress anchoring' so their traffic keeps the same source IP after we install. Need a clear shipping path.
tara: Agreed. Propose three delivery lanes: installer-lens (preflight + minimal operator), relay-fallback (for NATed sites), and airgap-bundle (offline + KMS/HSM).
lee: Installer-lens should include an egress validation step and CA import step. Preflight must fail fast with clear remediation steps.
nana: (typo: ana) Customers also want upgrade windows with non-disruptive rollbacks. Suggest a "canary sash" rollout: staged daemonset with health probes and quick rollback flag.
ev an: Can we quantify launch gates? My draft: minimal ship = installer-lens + docs; canary = 3 customers + telemetry; GA = documented rollback playbook + 90-day support SLA.
tara: Acceptance criteria suggestion: upgrade success >=97% in harness, rollback median <6m, preflight pass rate >98% internally.
lee: For egress anchoring: operator will attempt host-source preservation; if behind NAT, fallback to relay with perf budgets. Need perf targets: relay P95 token added latency <40ms.
nana: Who owns what? evan: roadmap + docs, tara: installer changes + preflight, lee: operator + relay perf, ana: field comms + canary signups.
build-bot: CI note: nightly build can run installer-lens preflight tests starting 2024-07-15.
ev an: Timeline: 1-week spike for operator prototype, 2-week sprint to add preflight + docs, 2-week canary. Aim for initial canary by end of quarter.
tara: I'll open the installer PR tomorrow. Lee, can you sketch the relay perf harness?
lee: Yep, will post draft perf tests by Wednesday.
ev an: Final: please ack owners here so product can lock launch gates by Monday.
